clue.text: Who might deliver text on court working?

definitions.text: Who might deliver text on court working?

parts.note: prose is written text

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of court are being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who reads out written material while active in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSE is followed by CUTOR, the letters of 'court' rearranged as 'working' signals; the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the lawyer who presents the case against the accused, delivering prepared statements in court.

clue.text: Elegant dog trade deal curtailed by UK and Italy

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sale is a trade deal
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A graceful hound changes hands in a cut-down deal between Britain and Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' docks the E from SALE, giving SAL, before UK and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender, graceful sighthound from the Middle East, noted for its elegance.

clue.text: US city turning up in South Carolina agreement

indicators.note: in places the reversed city inside the state's letters

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: NY stands for New York

explanation.surface: A big American city appears in a southern state's accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses NY to YN, which goes 'in' SC.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in sync is to be in harmony or accord, so the word stands for agreement or matching.

clue.text: Friends at school caught on carpet being hugged by girls

indicators.note: in a down entry a thing placed on another rests above it, so the letter named first sits on top of everything that follows

parts.note: c is caught on a cricket scorecard, written beside the dismissed batter's name

indicators.note: a hug closes right round whatever it holds, so the word after it opens to take in the letters named before

parts.note: lasses are girls, and the six letters part after the fourth
a mat is the small carpet laid inside a door

explanation.surface: Somebody caught on the carpet in the middle of a hug from a crowd of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the carpet' is the phrase the surface wants, meaning hauled up for a telling-off, and the carpet here is only a doormat. The cricketer's C has to sit above all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Classmates are the children who share a form room day after day, and school friendship is mostly made among them, which is the sense the definition leans on.

clue.text: Comedy series almost left on a high point?

indicators.note: in a down clue the shortened word sits on top of the next piece
almost the whole word: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a ridge is a raised stretch of high ground

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a sitcom has almost peaked, a high point nearly reached.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE was a classic BBC prison sitcom starring Ronnie Barker; 'porridge' is also British slang for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is the title of a much-loved British television sitcom set in a prison.

clue.text: Gangsters upset over British weapon

indicators.note: something upset has been tipped over, and in a down entry letters tipped over are read from the bottom up
in a down entry what is over a thing stands above it, so the letters just turned go on top of the one that follows

parts.note: a crowd of gangsters is a mob, written upwards
B is the standard single letter for British

explanation.surface: A crowd of gangsters furious about something British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as annoyed in the surface and means tipped over in the wordplay. Down entries turn upwards, so a reversal there is read from the bottom of the grid towards the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb is the plainest sort of weapon there is, a case of explosive dropped, thrown or planted to go off.

clue.text: A top year, with King throttled at an early stage

parts.note: the clue's own first letter, taken as it stands

indicators.note: to throttle somebody is to take them by the throat, and whatever is gripped that way is held inside the letters doing the gripping

parts.note: the lead is the top place in a race or a table, and the word opens after its first letter
R is Rex, the Latin king that follows a monarch's name on coins and signatures
y is the everyday short form of year

explanation.surface: A vintage year for the man out in front, until the king got both hands round his throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A top year' reads as praise for a vintage and is three separate pieces. R for Rex is the crossword's king, from the Elizabeth R of a royal signature, and the throttling buries it inside the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done already has been done sooner than anyone expected, which is to say at an early stage of whatever is going on.

clue.text: Blood flow issue? I start receiving treatment with O — one's injected

indicators.note: a patient receiving treatment is being worked on and comes out altered, so the letters beside it are re-set in another order
what is injected is driven into something already there, so the extra letter joins the pool before it is stirred

parts.note: anagram fodder, six letters
the clue's own letter, added to the mix
one written as the Roman numeral, the eighth letter for the mix

explanation.surface: A patient beginning a course of treatment, put on oxygen and then given an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is the only thing separating three lots of fodder, and every word around them is instruction rather than material. Aortitis is inflammation of the aorta, the great vessel blood leaves the heart through.
explanation.definitionFit: Aortitis is inflammation of the aorta, the artery every drop of blood leaves the heart by, so trouble there is an issue with the blood's flow.

clue.text: Barbarian suppressing old agreement? Take care

indicators.note: to suppress a thing is to hold it down out of sight, and what is held down stays inside the letters doing the holding

parts.note: a lout is an oafish barbarian, and the word opens after its first letter
O is the usual single letter for old
an OK given is an agreement, the word people say to settle a thing

explanation.surface: A brute sitting on an agreement made long ago, and a warning attached to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate short pieces go in together, which is why the middle of the answer reads as nothing in particular. The definition is an exclamation, shouted at somebody about to step off the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: Look out is what you shout at someone in danger, and take care is the same instruction given more quietly: both tell a person to watch what is coming.

clue.text: Cotton on rug after end of needlepoint

indicators.note: the wig comes after the letter from needlepoint
the end of needlepoint is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of needlepoint
rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: A sewing scene: cotton thread laid on a rug once the needlepoint is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' looks like thread in the sewing picture, but it is the phrasal verb meaning to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British for grasping or realising something, just as cotton on means to understand.

clue.text: Reservation about bad church money

definitions.note: The answer is plural and 'money' a mass noun: the funds a person can call on are counted as a set of holdings, and the setter names the stuff instead of the count.

indicators.note: what goes about a thing is wrapped round it, so the word before it parts and everything else is written between its halves

parts.note: res is the everyday short form of a reservation, and the three letters split before the last
milk that has gone bad has gone sour
CE is the Church of England, the church a British setter means when no other is named

explanation.surface: A doubt raised about a badly run church and the state of its finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' looks like the doubt the surface needs and is the booking, shortened. Sour for bad and CE for church are both worth banking, because they turn up in every other puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Somebody's resources are the funds and means at their disposal, so money is the commonest of them and stands for the lot.

clue.text: Priest, senior religious figure not using Old Testament in scripture lessons

indicators.note: a word not using something goes without it, so the two letters named next are struck out of the word before them

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the scripture lesson on a British school timetable, and the two letters part

indicators.note: what is in a thing sits inside it, so what is left over goes within the letters that follow

parts.note: an abbot is the head of a monastery, and he is the word being worked on
OT is the Old Testament, and these are the two letters struck out

explanation.surface: Clergy of two kinds in a scripture class where the Old Testament has been left off the syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbot is not a second man in the room, he is the word being cut about, and what survives drops into the lesson. RI is religious instruction, the British timetable's name for scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is the ordained teacher and leader of a Jewish congregation, the office 'priest' names loosely when it means whoever conducts the worship.

clue.text: Move slowly? That is fine at the top level

parts.note: to inch forward is to move a little at a time
i.e. is id est, the Latin for that is
F is fine on a pencil, the grade stamped along the barrel

explanation.surface: Somebody explaining that creeping along is perfectly acceptable at the highest level.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing is hidden, turned or shuffled: three everyday pieces in the order the clue sets them down. The answer only ever appears tacked onto a rank, as in commander-in-chief or editor-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: In chief is tacked onto a rank to mark its holder the most senior of them, as a commander-in-chief outranks every other commander.

clue.text: Subject losing head during brief romance? That's gratifying

indicators.note: during means the shortened subject comes within the brief romance

parts.note: a fling is a brief romance

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for subject is dropped

parts.note: a subject is a matter under discussion

explanation.surface: Someone finds it pleasing to be the subject of a brief romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' is a topic under discussion, not a monarch's subject, and the romance is brief by nature rather than shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flattering pleases your vanity and is gratifying to hear.

clue.text: Fashion stone without much skill

definitions.note: The answer is an adjective and the definition a phrase: a modest talent is one there is not much of, so the setter defines the word by what it says about the noun beside it.

parts.note: the mode is the prevailing fashion, the word taken straight from the French
st is the stone, the fourteen-pound unit the British still weigh themselves in

explanation.surface: Shaping a block of stone with no great craftsmanship about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' reads as the verb, shaping something by hand, and means the noun, the style of the moment. The stone is the weight on the bathroom scales rather than the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest income or a modest gift is one there is not a great deal of, so somebody of modest skill has little of it.

clue.text: Wasted away after soprano harboured hidden emotions

indicators.note: what comes after a thing follows it, so in a down entry the longer word is written below the letter already given

parts.note: S is soprano, the top line on a choir's score
something left to moulder has rotted quietly away

explanation.surface: A soprano keeping her feelings to herself, and pining away once she had.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to three words and sits at the very end, which is what makes the join so hard to find. To smoulder is to burn without flame, in a grate or in a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who smouldered went on burning without showing a flame, keeping anger or longing alive under the surface instead of letting it out.

clue.text: Narrowing of passage on sites rebuilt after end of hostilities

indicators.note: the final letter comes after the rearranged letters
rebuilt means these letters are put together again in a new order
the end of hostilities is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of hostilities

explanation.surface: Post-war reconstruction: a passage narrowed on building sites rebuilt once fighting stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenosis is the medical term for an abnormal constriction of a duct, vessel or other bodily channel.

clue.text: Completing the tour with nothing else to do?

definitions.meaning: read as the end of a package holiday, the itinerary worked down until only the final seaside town is left
read as empty days on your hands, and meant as having no other course open to you

explanation.surface: The tail end of a package holiday, with the days gone empty.
explanation.walkthrough: There is nothing to take apart into letters: the whole phrase carries two readings, and the enumeration is the only real help. The noun is a seaside town in one of them and a course of action in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In the last resort means when every other course has failed, and the same words place you in the final holiday town of a tour.

clue.text: Hope stimulated around university — upturn in attitude — feeling of wellbeing

indicators.note: around puts the rearranged letters on either side of the university letter
stimulated suggests the letters of hope are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the word from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: Optimism at a university is given a boost, lifting the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stimulated' turns HOPE into EPHO, which goes 'around' U for EUPHO; 'upturn in' reverses AIR to RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is an intense state of happiness and elation, a strong sense of wellbeing.

clue.text: Prepare mine for a fight in unpleasant place

parts.note: to arm is to prepare, as for battle
a pit is both a mine and the arena where animals are set to fight, as in a cockpit or bear pit

explanation.surface: Someone readies an explosive mine for combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a fight' seems to say why the mine is armed, but it belongs with 'mine': a pit is a coal mine and also a fighting arena.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is a sweaty, smelly part of the body, and figuratively the most disagreeable spot somewhere.

clue.text: Recalled report, containing ordinary lines almost bursting with content?

indicators.note: containing means the reversed word holds the other letters inside it
recalled is read as called back, so the word runs in reverse

parts.note: news is a report of events

explanation.surface: A withdrawn report held ordinary lines and seemed full to the brim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses NEWS to SWEN, which is 'containing' O and LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swollen is distended and puffed out, as though stuffed nearly to the point of splitting.

clue.text: Love judge imprisoning Duke, alas

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis, written as a nought

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut a thing up inside walls, so the letter named next is locked within the word before it

parts.note: a court hears a case, which is how a judge judges it, and the word opens after its first letter
D is the standard single letter for duke

explanation.surface: A judge sending a duke to prison, with love in the case somewhere and a sigh over the whole thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love judge' reads as one phrase, a magistrate hearing a romance, and is two pieces that have nothing to do with each other. The definition is an exclamation, which is why the answer is one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas and oh dear are both what a person says when something has gone wrong, the first out of a book and the second out of anybody's mouth.

clue.text: Pulled up trees, very pleased with oneself

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: gums are eucalyptus trees

explanation.surface: Someone who uprooted trees is feeling self-satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: Gum trees are eucalypts, so 'trees' gives GUMS, and 'Pulled up' reads it from the bottom of this down light upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes complacent self-satisfaction, an excessive pride in one's own achievements.

clue.text: Slicing this fruit could make chap pee

definitions.text: Slicing this fruit could make chap pee

parts.note: a chap is a man
to go is a euphemism for urinating, to pee

explanation.surface: A cheeky warning that cutting up some fruit might make a man need the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: cut the fruit's name in two and the halves read as 'chap' and 'pee'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit whose name splits neatly into two everyday words.

clue.text: Some appellation in Appendix?

indicators.note: some of a thing is a part of it and never the whole, so only a short run of the letters that follow is wanted

parts.note: the run starts on the last letter of the first word, takes the short one whole and stops one letter into the last

explanation.surface: A name turning up somewhere in the appendix at the back of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight the clue says what the answer is and where it is: a name, and one buried in the words themselves. Setters call a message hidden in a grid a nina, after the cartoonist Al Hirschfeld, who drew his daughter's name into his pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina is a girl's name, which is all an appellation is, and the clue's own words hold the letters, so the sentence describes itself as much as the answer.

clue.text: Source of venison? Various diners always tucking in

indicators.note: tucking in places the poetic word inside the rearranged letters
various suggests the letters of diners in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Diners of every sort are forever tucking in, asking where the venison comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' turns DINERS into REINDS; E'ER goes inside, 'tucking in' between REIND and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is deer meat, and reindeer are among the deer hunted or farmed for it.

clue.text: Attempt to support one American villain in theatre

indicators.note: what supports a thing holds it up from underneath, so in a down entry the piece named first goes at the bottom

parts.note: one written as the Roman numeral
A is the standard single letter for American
a go at something is an attempt at it

explanation.surface: An attempt to prop up a single American, and a stage villain into the bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The only instruction in the clue is 'support', and in a down entry that sends the attempt underneath rather than in front. Iago is the ensign who talks Othello into murdering his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago poisons Othello's mind against Desdemona through five acts of Shakespeare's play, which makes him the theatre's byword for a villain.

clue.text: Eating out, consuming new herb

indicators.note: consuming means the rearranged letters take the new letter inside
out suggests the letters of eating are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone dining out tries a novel herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EATING to GETIAN, which is 'consuming' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentian is a flowering plant whose bitter root is used as a medicinal herb and in tonics.

clue.text: Turning to observe, being in pursuit of the very best beards

indicators.note: being in pursuit of means the reversed word follows behind the other piece

parts.note: GOAT is slang for the greatest of all time

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to see is to observe

explanation.surface: Turning to look at the champions, one notices their facial hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses SEE to EES, which comes after GOAT, 'being in pursuit of' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard on the chin, so the plural names such beards.
